stem: A community paediatric trainee reviews a child with injuries concerning for maltreatment, but the history is incomplete and collateral information is still being gathered; what is the best principle for mandatory reporting decisions?

options.text: A report should wait until a complete investigation has been performed
A report can be made once there is a reasonable level of suspicion based on clinical acumen
A report should only be made after the Child Protection Unit has confirmed maltreatment
A report should only be made if the child discloses abuse directly
A report should be deferred until police have identified the person causing harm

explanation: A report can be made once there is a reasonable level of suspicion based on clinical acumen. Mandatory reporting does not require a complete investigation, confirmed maltreatment, or direct disclosure before action is taken.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a complete investigation is not required before filing a report.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the reporting threshold is a reasonable level of suspicion based on clinical acumen, and reporting should not be delayed for full confirmation.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because confirmation by the Child Protection Unit is not required before making a report.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the threshold is reasonable suspicion, not a direct disclosure from the child.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because police identification of the person causing harm is not required before reporting.
